name: Provalume design tokens
identity: light-first, warm, archival. Dark is an override, never the default.
authority: This file is the single source of truth. tokens.css, the Rich terminal theme, and generated HTML all derive from these names. See ADR-0018.

green.role: primary functional accent: actions, links, success

mauve.role: secondary categories, lineage, provenance and supersession chains

gold.role: verified, promoted, attested, trusted states. Used sparingly.

accessibility.verified_by: docs/design/contrast_check.py — runs in CI, exits non-zero on violation
accessibility.never_color_alone: Every trust state carries a text label. The system must be readable in a monochrome terminal, by a colour-blind reader, and when piped to a file.

constraints.detail: gold on warm-white measures 3.04:1 — below the 4.5:1 AA threshold for normal text. Gold is permitted only for badges, large text (>=18.66px bold or >=24px), icons, and borders.
gold on beige-light measures 2.70:1 and on beige-soft 2.40:1 — below the 3.0:1 non-text threshold. Gold must not appear on either beige. Gold badges sit on warm-white or white.
Because of the two rules above, the verified state renders as a gold-bordered badge on white with a black text label — not as gold prose.

typography.family.sans: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
typography.family.mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace
typography.family.serif: ui-serif, Georgia, Cambria, 'Times New Roman', serif
typography.large-text-threshold: 18.66px bold or 24px regular — the boundary where gold becomes permissible

iconography.direction: lineage and branching paths, archival records and ledgers, evidence seals, cairns and stacked-stone markers, provenance nodes, verified check-marks inside a bordered field
iconography.reasoning: The mark should read 'this was recorded and it holds up', not 'an AI did something'. See ADR-0001 and ADR-0018.

terminal.notes: Rich styles derive from the semantic roles above. Terminal colour rendering is approximate, so state is always labelled in text and colour is reinforcement only.
rules: No background fills — the user's terminal background is theirs.
NO_COLOR and non-TTY output are honoured, producing plain text.
Every trust state prints its name, never colour alone.

dark.rule: If added, it is an override triggered by prefers-color-scheme: dark or data-theme="dark", mapping the same semantic role names to dark-appropriate values. Light remains the canonical identity: screenshots, social previews, and documentation default to light.
